user_actions_needed: Keep the TV pairing as is. The PC is already paired as client name 'Lumen Remote' (token saved today in lumen-remote/data/tv.json). Do not rename the client. Back up data/tv.json as a secret.

On the TV, set Settings > General > External Device Manager > Device Connection Manager > Access Notification to 'First Time Only' (not Off), and confirm 'Lumen Remote' is listed as Allow in Device List. Otherwise the Allow prompt may reappear after power cycles.
Turn on Settings > General > Network > Expert Settings > Power On with Mobile (needed for Wake-on-LAN and cloud power-on). Tell me if the option is missing on this Indian-region firmware.

To get real picture levels (Brightness/backlight, contrast, colour tone, etc.): turn on Settings > General > Network > Expert Settings > IP Remote. Then, when nobody is watching, approve the one-time 'IP Remote permission' dialog on the TV within about 30-60 s while I pair on port 1516 (confirmed open today). Tell me if IP Remote is not in the menu.

Schedule a supervised test session of about 30-45 minutes with no one watching. It covers: a first reversible SetVolume +1 test; a key lab at 1 key/second for unverified keys (HDMI, picture size, caption, ambient, 123/More); an IME replace-vs-append test; a standby/Wake-on-LAN cycle; the on-TV avocd D-Bus read probe (introspect the TV's own picture service and read Brightness while you move the slider); the MobileBFF probe; and recording the Settings menu layout for macros.

When the Windows Security Alert for node.exe appears (only after you enable 'live events' or 'phone access'), click Allow and tick the Private profile; make sure the home network is set to Private. Cancel or X creates permanent block rules that need an administrator to remove. Optionally run one elevated command for a narrow rule limited to the TV.

Decide whether the on-TV Lumen Agent may be updated and launched by the remote. It reuses the installed lumenrmt01 package, installs over the same sdb link as the CineHD pipeline, and when re-armed it briefly appears on screen. Approve each install, ideally outside CineHD deploys.

Decide on SmartThings (optional, cloud, paid API plans announced from October 2026). If you want friendly HDMI names, cloud power-on or the picture-mode fallback: confirm the TV is in your SmartThings account, accept or decline the possible $4.99/month plan, and create an OAuth-In app with the SmartThings CLI (I will supply the exact app.json), then authorise it and paste the returned code.
Tell me which device is on HDMI1 (the only connected HDMI port) and whether a set-top box needs channel keys through Anynet+/HDMI-CEC, so input names and channel controls behave correctly.

Decide on opt-in extras: phone access over the LAN (PIN pairing; plain http, so no phone PWA unless you accept a local certificate), YouTube now-playing through the Lounge API (may show a 'device connected' toast on the TV), and whether CineHD's MediaService may publish now-playing to the remote.
Optional: enter the TV's rated power in watts for the energy estimate, and the volume cap you want (default 50).
open_risks: Backlight and the per-field picture values are documented in Samsung's 2020 IP command list and 1516 is open, but no 2020 field report confirms backlightControl returns a real value; a 2018 set returns -32003, and the IN-region menu may lack the IP Remote item. If IP Control falls short, the avocd D-Bus path (also unverified on real firmware; may be blocked by a shipped D-Bus/cynara policy) or menu macros + TRACKED values are the fallbacks.

The avocd D-Bus read path rests on static analysis of the Dec-2019 x86 emulator image, not the TV's 2026 armv7 firmware. Real firmware could enforce a D-Bus policy, rename the service, or require a privilege the distributor certificate cannot grant. It needs one supervised read-only probe before anything depends on it.

GENA change events are verified, but only while CineHD and Netflix were both background. Change events from inside a foreground app, and HDMI-vs-TV sources, were not observed; the single-master-volume assumption is likely but unproven.

Windows Firewall: a cancelled prompt, or an Allow that leaves the active profile unticked, creates permanent node.exe block rules; GENA push and phone access then fail silently until an administrator removes them. The design detects this and falls back to polling.

KEY_POWER is a toggle; stale state or a repeat inside the 5-20 s lag window can turn the TV back on, and a ~5 s hold soft-resets it. Mitigated by fresh REST checks, cooldowns and Click-only sends, but inherently racy.
Opening the WebSocket can wake some TVs; any path that opens it as a probe or reconnects in standby could switch the TV on unexpectedly.
The REST API serialises requests (~1.35 s per app query) and never answers unknown or slash-less paths; careless polling makes the UI lag and loads the TV while someone is watching.

Companion limits: the service context has no TV APIs (confirmed), hidden UI JavaScript is paused, the service may be frozen ~10 s after the UI hides or killed in standby, there is no boot autostart, and re-arming flashes the screen and may pause playback. Lifetime is only measured to 2.4 s.
tizen.tvchannel and webapis.hybridchannelinfo work on this firmware despite being removed from Samsung's docs; a firmware update could remove them, so guard every call.
Menu-navigation macros are fragile: the layout changes with input, HDR, Game Mode, picture mode and firmware, the TV reports no cursor position, keys can drop, and values they set are only TRACKED.

MobileBFF is unprobed; whether it answers over the paired MSF link on 2020 firmware, whether it raises an Allow prompt, and which vconf keys it permits are all open. It cannot provide picture levels regardless.
SmartThings: 402 from October 2026, 24 h personal tokens, single-use refresh tokens, a 12/min limit, stale state, and commands that report success without applying — a weak, optional layer.
Volume and mute from UPnP or IP Control reflect only the TV-speaker path; with ARC/eARC/optical/Bluetooth output they can be meaningless or refused (-32002), and the UI must say so.
Text input works only in native Tizen keyboard fields (not YouTube/Prime), and imeUpdate can expose plaintext from password fields, so it must never be logged or broadcast.

Privacy: REST, UPnP descriptions, DIAL (YouTube screenId), SmartThings deviceinfo, IP Control getDeviceInformation and MobileBFF network vconf all return identifiers (MACs, SSID/BSSID, DUID, serial, developerIP). Any logging or screenshot path that misses the redaction filter would leak them.
Security: once IP Remote is enabled, anything on the LAN that pairs can control power and settings; the PC host becomes a LAN attack surface in phone mode, served over plain http.

The TLS fingerprint pin is probably identical across this TV generation (the key ships in firmware), so it only protects against casual interception; IP Control weak-DH settings must stay scoped to that one connection.

Evidence for pairing and the companion (lumen-remote/data/*) was recorded today by another session, and the TV, sdb link and CineHD app (now 0.17.421) are shared; parallel work on the same TV can collide.
